# My Thinking

I've farmed this land in Quzhou for over 30 years. The North China Plain is what it is — limited rain, hot summers, cold winters. My father grew wheat and maize here, and so do I, because the soil, the water, the markets, and the government support all point the same direction. I'm not going to reinvent anything at 59.

My 10 mu goes into the standard double-crop rotation: winter wheat sown in October, harvested in June, then summer maize goes straight in behind it, harvested by October. Same land, two harvests. That's how you make this land pay.

I've been farming long enough to know over-fertilizing is wasteful and hurts the soil. I've also watched the water table drop my whole adult life. I'll irrigate wheat three times — the pre-winter water is non-negotiable for root establishment, then jointing and grain-filling. Maize I'll irrigate once unless the July rains fail badly. I won't pump more than I need.

For varieties, I use Jimai series wheat and Xianyu 335 maize — proven, high-yielding, adapted to this county. No gambling on untested material at my age. Rotary till before wheat to break up the stubble. For maize I go straight in with no-tillage — saves fuel, holds moisture, and I've seen it works.

Pesticide: herbicide in autumn for the wheat, fungicide at heading to guard against scab, maybe one more spray if aphids come in spring. Maize gets herbicide and I watch for borer. That's it.
